about: Signals: announcements, commitments, gatherings and findings that show which way heat policy and practice are moving in South and Southeast Asia. A commitment climbs a ladder (announced, adopted, funded, delivered, evaluated) and each move is dated in its history; an announcement is a weak signal, and each rung is stronger evidence that change is real. Every signal reuses a source the site has already checked, or passed its own check (research/2026-11/signals-cop31/). The ladder records how far each signal has got, never how well an institution performs. Checked by build-data.js --check.

ladder.label: Announced
ladder.means: Said in public. A weak signal on its own: announcements happen whether or not anything follows.

ladder.label: Adopted
ladder.means: Made formal: a plan approved, a rule changed, an office set up.

ladder.label: Funded
ladder.means: Money committed to it, whether or not the amount is public.

ladder.label: Delivered
ladder.means: Something exists that people can use: a service open, a guide published, money paid out.

ladder.label: Evaluated
ladder.means: Its results were measured and published.

kinds.label: Commitment
kinds.means: Something an institution has promised or started; it climbs the ladder.

kinds.label: Gathering
kinds.means: A conference or forum where the field meets; what it produces may become commitments.

kinds.label: Finding
kinds.means: New science that changes how heat is understood.

kinds.label: Guidance
kinds.means: A framework or guide published for others to use.

groups.label: COP31 watch
groups.intro: What we are watching for heat at COP31. Each item is added only after its source passes the site's check, on the rung it has truly reached; almost everything at a conference starts as an announcement.

groups.label: Signals of the year
groups.intro: This year's signals already on Common Shade, each with the source the site checked.

signals.title: COP31 opens in Antalya
signals.summary: COP31, the UN climate conference, is held in Antalya from 9 to 20 November 2026.
signals.next: Watch for heat in its outcomes on adaptation, health, finance, cooling and early warnings; each enters this page on the rung it has truly reached.

sources.label: UNFCCC: UN Climate Change Conference, Antalya, November 2026

signals.title: 2026 will be one of the four warmest years on record
signals.summary: WMO's State of the Climate Update 2026, released as COP31 opened, finds that the past 12 years have each been the warmest on record and the past four the top four. The global average surface temperature for January to September 2026 was about 1.47 °C above the pre-industrial average. In early November the EU's Copernicus service said 2026 is most likely to be the second-hottest year on record.
signals.next: A finding, not a commitment: watch whether heat plans and budgets are sized for the heat these years now bring, not the heat people remember.

sources.label: WMO, 2026: State of the climate in 2026 gives new meaning to phrase 'off the charts'
WMO: State of the Climate Update for COP31
AFP via The Korea Times, 2026: 2026 most likely to be second-hottest year on record

signals.title: El Niño set to bring more heat into 2027
signals.summary: By mid-August 2026 El Niño had become firmly established. WMO reports it has been intensifying since August and is expected to be the strongest on record by December, set to unleash even more heat and extreme weather well into 2027.
signals.next: What to watch: early warnings and heat plans ready for the 2027 hot season, above all in Southeast Asia, where El Niño and warming broke records in April 2016.

sources.label: WMO, 2026: State of the climate in 2026 gives new meaning to phrase 'off the charts'
WMO: El Niño/La Niña Update, August 2026

signals.title: Warming will overshoot 1.5 °C: the Emissions Gap Report 2026
signals.summary: UNEP's Emissions Gap Report 2026, The Point of Return, finds that with global temperature rise set to exceed 1.5 °C, urgent and stringent cuts are needed to minimise the size and length of the overshoot and return to 1.5 °C by the end of the century. If current policies continue, warming could reach 2.8 °C this century; if all national pledges are delivered, 2.6 °C.
signals.who: UNEP, with PBL Netherlands Environmental Assessment Agency
signals.next: A finding, not a commitment: watch whether adaptation plans for heat assume the warming these projections describe.

sources.label: PBL Netherlands Environmental Assessment Agency: UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2026

signals.title: 59 Belém Adaptation Indicators to measure progress on adaptation
signals.summary: At the 2025 UN climate conference (CMA 7), countries adopted a set of 59 Belém Adaptation Indicators to measure progress towards the targets for adaptation; reporting on them will serve as an input to the global stocktake.

history.note: Adopted at CMA 7, under the Global Goal on Adaptation

signals.next: Delivered: countries in South and Southeast Asia reporting on the indicators, including those that touch heat and health.

sources.label: UNFCCC: Global Goal on Adaptation

signals.title: India adds heatwaves to its notified natural calamities
signals.summary: In August 2026 India added heatwaves to its notified natural calamities, so national and state disaster response funds can pay for heatwave relief. Before, states could spend only up to 10% of their response fund on locally declared disasters such as heat. Heat mitigation projects are funded separately, from disaster mitigation funds.

history.note: A rule change, reported from a reply in India's Lok Sabha

signals.next: Funded and delivered: heatwave relief paid from a state or national response fund, and reported.

sources.label: Down To Earth, 2026: India updates disaster list to include heatwaves and lightning

signals.title: The first Global Heat Forum, in Bangkok
signals.summary: Nearly 600 scientists, business leaders, philanthropists and health experts met in Bangkok from 6 to 9 October 2026. The Forum released the first country-level heat and health assessments for Bangladesh, Bhutan, India and Nepal, and a roadmap for investment and action on extreme heat.
signals.next: Watch for the roadmap's investments to become funded commitments.

sources.label: ClimateWorks Foundation, 2026: Global Heat Forum gathers 600 leaders

signals.title: Bangladesh's first urban heatwave action plan, for Narayanganj
signals.summary: Narayanganj City Corporation's heat action plan was approved on 22 September 2025 and published in 2026. It gives each short-term action a tentative cost in taka and names potential funding sources, often development partners and NGOs.
signals.next: Funded: budget lines for its actions, from the city or its partners.

sources.label: Narayanganj City Corporation: Heat Action Plan, 2025
Prothom Alo, 2026: Bangladesh's first urban heatwave action plan

signals.title: Bangladesh adopts its Health National Adaptation Plan
signals.summary: Bangladesh adopted its Health National Adaptation Plan 2026. It estimates about US$1.4 billion is needed over five years, and plans to draw on public budgets through a climate fiscal framework and on international climate funds such as the Adaptation Fund and the GCF.
signals.next: Funded: money committed against its five-year costing.

sources.label: UNFPA Bangladesh, 2026: adoption of the Health National Adaptation Plan
Government of Bangladesh: Health National Adaptation Plan 2026

signals.title: Bangkok's heat plan opens 304 cooling centres
signals.summary: For the 2026 hot season Bangkok opened 304 cooling centres in schools, health centres and district offices. The city's own Urban Heat Management Action Plan for 2026 has 22 indicators, and a 2026 financing strategy with UNDP costs it at about THB 146 million to set up and THB 10.8 million a year to run, noting that running costs are not always covered.

history.note: The city's Urban Heat Management Action Plan for 2026
304 cooling centres open for the hot season

signals.next: Evaluated: who used the cooling centres, and with what result.

signals.title: Singapore sets up a Heat Resilience Policy Office and funds heat research
signals.summary: In March 2026 a Heat Resilience Policy Office was set up to coordinate action across agencies, oversee research and draft a heat resilience action plan. A S$40 million 'Adapting to Heat Impacts' funding initiative supports research on heat impacts and community heat resilience.
signals.who: Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment, Singapore
signals.next: Delivered: the heat resilience action plan the office is drafting.

sources.label: Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment, Singapore: Committee of Supply 2026

signals.title: A South Asia climate-health desk and a heat research consortium
signals.summary: Announced on 20 February 2026: The Rockefeller Foundation and Wellcome fund a South Asia Climate-Health Desk under the WHO-WMO Climate and Health Joint Programme, and a South Asia Scientific Research Consortium, through a Rockefeller grant to IISER Pune, to develop tailored heat-risk thresholds. Amounts were not disclosed.
signals.next: Delivered: tailored heat-risk thresholds published for use in warnings.

sources.label: WMO, 2026: new initiatives launched to address extreme heat in South Asia

signals.title: Support for the Southeast Asia Heat Health Hub's next stage
signals.summary: Announced on 8 October 2026: support for the next stage of the Global Heat Health Information Network's Southeast Asia Hub, including funding for heat-health work in Indonesia (Makassar and two more cities) and Thailand in 2027, and preparations for a second Southeast Asia Heat Health Forum. The amount was not disclosed.
signals.next: Delivered: heat-health work under way in Indonesia and Thailand in 2027.

sources.label: Philanthropy Asia Alliance, via Eco-Business, 2026

signals.title: April's pre-monsoon heatwave was made three times more likely
signals.summary: Fifteen days of heat in late April 2026 pushed India's electricity demand to a record and brought farm drought to more than a million square kilometres. Scientists found climate change made it three times more likely, and that April heat like this now returns about every five years.
signals.next: A finding, not a commitment: watch whether plans are sized to heat that now returns about every five years.

sources.label: World Weather Attribution, 2026
Mongabay, 2026

signals.title: India's Heat Resilient Cities Framework
signals.summary: India's National Institute of Urban Affairs published a Heat Resilient Cities Framework: a yearly city intervention plan, and a long-term heat resilience perspective.
signals.who: National Institute of Urban Affairs, Climate Centre for Cities
signals.next: Watch for cities that adopt it in their own plans.
